# T5.06: GPU swizzle (measured, not adopted)

Question: would a GPU pass (IOSurface → NVENC's input layout) beat the CPU tiler?

`tools/gpuswizzle.m`: a Metal compute kernel (nullmoth's Metal over NVK) reads an IOSurface-backed NV12 pixel buffer,
as ScreenCaptureKit delivers, and writes NVENC's layout (64x16 tiles of 16x4 sub-blocks) into a shared `MTLBuffer`.
One thread per 16-byte run, inverse of `nvenc_in_offset`. Checked byte for byte against `nvenc_in_tile_plane`:
**0 mismatching runs**, both versions.

| 3840x2160 NV12 | time |
|---|---|
| kernel v1: IOSurface planes as R8/RG8 textures, 16 single-byte reads per thread | 67 ms GPU (72 ms wall) |
| kernel v2: IOSurface wrapped as an MTLBuffer (`newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`), one 16-byte load + store per thread | **1.66 ms GPU, 1.88 ms wall** (submit + wait) |
| CPU tiler (`nvenc_in_tile_plane`, SSE, 2 threads), warm | 0.65 ms (tilebench); **0.87 ms inside Parsec** |

Why the GPU loses here: on this driver IOSurfaces and mapped buffers live in system RAM ("LOCAL+mapped memory → system
RAM"), so the kernel moves 12 MB in and 12 MB out over PCIe 4.0 x8, while the CPU tiles the same 12 MB from RAM it reads
at memory speed. The GPU path would add ~1 ms of latency per 4K frame and save ~0.9 ms of CPU (2.6 % of one core at 30
fps).

Not adopted. The remaining steps (import the MTLBuffer's pages into our RM client with `NV01_MEMORY_SYSTEM_OS_DESCRIPTOR`,
host-pointer import; order the Metal command buffer before the NVENC submit) only make sense if capture surfaces move to
VRAM (a driver change), so NVENC could read a GPU-resident frame directly, as on Windows. `gpuswizzle` stays as the
starting point for that.
